title: Early onset of spring increases the phenological mismatch between plants and pollinators
screening_reason: Direct multi-year plant-pollinator phenology matched to seed-set outcome in the same populations; primary Tier-A candidate.
notes: Corydalis ambigua × overwintered Bombus queens; 3 populations, 10-14 years. Raw/supporting data route reported. Dependence with IWE002/IWE003 must be resolved before pooling.

title: When spring ephemerals fail to meet pollinators: mechanism of phenological mismatch and its impact on plant reproduction
screening_reason: Direct 19-year mismatch-to-seed-production relationship plus snow-removal experiment; primary Tier-A candidate.
notes: Corydalis ambigua × bumblebee queens. Likely overlaps biologically/data-wise with IWE001; assign shared dependence structure during extraction.

title: Site-specific variation in flowering phenology of a spring ephemeral plant and its implications for phenological mismatch with pollinators under climate change
screening_reason: Phenology, bumblebee availability and seed set are measured, but overlap with earlier Corydalis datasets and extractable independent mismatch effect require full-text adjudication.
notes: 2026 Corydalis ambigua multi-population study; do not count independently until population/year overlap with IWE001/IWE002 is mapped.

title: How does timing of flowering affect competition for pollinators, flower visitation and seed set in an early spring grassland plant?
screening_reason: Direct flowering timing, pollinator availability/visitation and seed-set outcomes in matched sites; raw-data route available; Tier-A candidate.
notes: Pulsatilla vulgaris across 8 grasslands. Construct synchrony exposure from matched plant and pollinator phenology rather than using visitation alone.

title: Pollinator effectiveness varies with experimental shifts in flowering time
screening_reason: Experimental flowering-time shifts with seed production after pollinator visits; direct reproductive response to altered timing; Tier-A candidate.
notes: Tradescantia ohiensis and Asclepias incarnata may provide separate biological units; dependence retained at publication/experiment level.

title: Effects of experimental shifts in flowering phenology on plant-pollinator interactions
screening_reason: Experimental flowering shifts measured pollinator visitation but not a final plant reproductive outcome meeting Tier-A criteria.
notes: Useful mechanism/context source for Rafferty programme; excluded from primary meta-analysis unless a qualifying reproductive outcome is recovered.

title: Warming of experimental plant-pollinator communities advances phenologies alters traits reduces interactions and depresses reproduction
screening_reason: Experimental warming changes phenology and seed reproduction but simultaneously alters multiple traits/resources; direct mismatch-specific effect must be isolated before Tier-A admission.
notes: Three annual plants plus solitary bee. Keep as sensitivity candidate for multi-mechanism timing manipulations.

title: Pollinator peaking earlier than flowering is more detrimental to plant fecundity
screening_reason: Explicit key-pollinator peak mismatch and seed-setting outcome at community scale; effect and sampling-variance extraction route still needs full-text/data adjudication.
notes: Qilian Mountains alpine grassland; potentially many plant-species effects with shared site/community dependence.

title: A specialist bee and its host plants experience phenological shifts at different rates in response to climate change
screening_reason: Occurrence-derived long-term plant and bee phenology illustrates mismatch potential but lacks matched plant reproductive fitness outcomes.
notes: Habropoda laboriosa × Vaccinium; retain as Tier-C/context reference not primary evidence.

title: Is increased male flower production a strategy for avoidance of predispersal seed predation in andromonoecious plants?
screening_reason: Strong direct seasonal enemy-window evidence but partner activity is not quantified as a matched population-year overlap exposure; use timing-sensitivity lane rather than strict H1.
notes: Peucedanum multivittatum × Phaulernis fulviguttella; Dryad 10.5061/dryad.b5mkkwhcq. Potential dependence with IWE011.

title: Phenological selection mosaic of predispersal seed predation affects gender variation in an andromonoecious plant
screening_reason: Four-year phenological selection mosaic and final fitness are strong seasonal-timing evidence but do not yet provide the same direct synchrony exposure as strict H1.
notes: Peucedanum multivittatum; likely partially overlaps IWE010 populations/years. Use timing-sensitivity/dependence-aware extraction only.

title: Caterpillar seed predators mediate shifts in selection on flowering phenology in their host plant
screening_reason: Seed predator presence shifts flowering-time selection but continuous partner-activity overlap is not measured; strong timing-sensitivity evidence rather than strict H1.
notes: Gentiana pneumonanthe × Phengaris alcon across 20 populations and 2 years.

title: Flowering schedule in a perennial plant; life-history trade-offs seed predation and total offspring fitness
screening_reason: Links flowering schedule seed predation and total offspring fitness but does not directly measure synchrony with predator phenology under the current strict primary definition.
notes: Actaea spicata; important evidence that antagonists alter optimal within-season timing retained for contextual synthesis.

title: Flower herbivory and seed predation in Silene vulgaris (Caryophyllaceae): effects of pollination and phenology
screening_reason: Same Hadena partners provide pollination and seed predation and seasonal phenology is linked to final seed set; recoverable quantitative synchrony effect and variance still need full-text adjudication.
notes: Do not promote solely because biology matches the hypothesis; source-level effect and variance remain unresolved.

title: Variable and sexually conflicting selection on Silene stellata floral traits by a putative moth pollinator selective agent
screening_reason: Early Hadena-dominant versus late co-pollinator-dominant windows provide direct seasonal timing and final fitness but not a quantitative synchrony metric; extracted to timing-sensitivity lane.
notes: Silene stellata × Hadena ectypa; Dryad 10.5061/dryad.6q573n5w1. Published uncertainty label is internally inconsistent with bounded outcomes and requires raw-data verification before quantitative pooling.

title: Interactions between a pollinating seed predator and its host plant: the role of environmental context within a population
screening_reason: Direct pollination and predation consequences are measured but the focal exposure is environmental/host-density context rather than phenological synchrony.
notes: Silene stellata × Hadena ectypa. Useful mechanistic/context source not primary IWE timing evidence.

title: Staying in touch: how highly specialised moth pollinators track host plant phenology in unpredictable climates
screening_reason: Direct host and Epicephala phenology quantifies tracking mechanisms but no matched synchrony-to-final-plant-fitness effect is provided.
notes: Breynia oblongifolia × Epicephala. Key context for specialization/tracking hypothesis not Tier-A fitness evidence.

title: An obligate pollination mutualism and reciprocal diversification in the tree genus Glochidion (Euphorbiaceae)
screening_reason: Establishes active pollination and seed-consumption biology with reproductive consequences but lacks variation in phenological synchrony as the focal exposure.
notes: Japanese Glochidion × Epicephala anchor; do not promote to synchrony evidence.

title: Competitive Exclusion among Fig Wasps Achieved via Entrainment of Host Plant Flowering Phenology
screening_reason: Measures host/wasp phenology and reports abortion under poorly matched crop timing but fit to plant reproductive-fitness estimand is unclear and male-fig/pollinator cycling dominates the design.
notes: Ficus pumila × Wiebesia spp.; full-text adjudication required before any Tier-A use.

title: Asymmetrical nature of the Trollius-Chiastocheta interaction: insights into the evolution of nursery pollination systems
screening_reason: Quantifies costs/benefits and seed set across fly-presence contexts but not a direct phenological synchrony exposure tied to plant fitness.
notes: Trollius europaeus × Chiastocheta; useful nursery-pollination background and net-effect context.

title: Retention of mutualism in a geographically diverging interaction
screening_reason: Measures Greya pollination effects and seed set across years but lacks a direct plant-partner synchrony exposure under the IWE primary estimand.
notes: Lithophragma cymbalaria × Greya spp.; relevant redundancy/context evidence not primary timing evidence.

title: Pollinators limit seed production in an early blooming rare plant: evidence of a mismatch between plant phenology and pollinator emergence
screening_reason: Seasonal bee captures flowering timing and viable-seed production are all available but must be matched at compatible location/time grain before a strict synchrony effect is admitted.
notes: Trifolium barnebyi × primarily Andrena bees; Dryad 10.5061/dryad.s4mw6m9bg contains hand-pollination Julian day seed outcomes and bee trapping dates.

title: Pollinator visitation rate and effectiveness vary with flowering phenology
screening_reason: Flowering onset was experimentally manipulated and final seed set measured; null/weak seed-set timing response is admissible and important for avoiding positive-result bias.
notes: Mertensia ciliata; four experimental flowering windows with pollinator composition/effectiveness and seed set; Dryad 10.7280/D19X0D.

title: Phenological change in a spring ephemeral: implications for pollination and plant reproduction
screening_reason: Snow-removal and greenhouse timing manipulations altered flowering phenology with pollinator visitation pollen limitation fruit set and seed set measured; strong Tier-A experimental candidate.
notes: Claytonia lanceolata; 2011-2013 snow manipulation plus 2013 early/control/late outdoor arrays.

title: Experimental Test of the Combined Effects of Water Availability and Flowering Time on Pollinator Visitation and Seed Set
screening_reason: Factorial experimental flowering-time manipulation measured seed set and seed mass; timing effect is directly estimable while water treatment is retained as crossed design/dependence.
notes: Mertensia ciliata; four phenology weeks × three water treatments. Dryad 10.7280/D16D7Z. Strict-window status depends on measured partner-availability ordering; otherwise direct-timing sensitivity.

title: Consequences of variation in flowering time within and among individuals of Mertensia fusiformis (Boraginaceae) an early spring wildflower
screening_reason: Flowering date total seed production and pollen limitation were measured across two contrasting years but explicit partner activity is not yet sufficient for a strict synchrony effect.
notes: Mertensia fusiformis; useful direct seasonal-timing candidate with frost confounding explicitly documented.

title: Flowering phenology influences seed production and outcrossing rate in populations of an alpine snowbed shrub Phyllodoce aleutica: effects of pollinators and self-incompatibility
screening_reason: Sequential flowering along snowmelt gradients was matched to seasonal bumblebee visitation and seed set across sites and years; observational Tier-A candidate.
notes: Phyllodoce aleutica; intact/emasculated seed set across early/mid/late plots at two sites in 2006-2007 and direct seasonal bumblebee visitation in 2007.

title: Flowering phenology and seed predation by a tephritid fly: Escape of seeds in time and space
screening_reason: Direct flowering-rank and seed-predator escape evidence is strong, but the accessible article/thesis programme does not provide an observed final-fitness response paired to a recoverable plant-partner matching metric with sampling variance.
notes: Tripolium vulgare × Paroxyna plantaginis; retain as high-information antagonist timing/escape context. Associated thesis models realized seed set from potential seed set and attack components rather than supplying the strict observed timing-to-fitness estimand.

title: Evolutionary consequences of flowering-pollinator asynchrony: the case of a floral oil-producing plant and its oil-collecting bees
screening_reason: Two within-season periods had strongly contrasting flowering-pollinator overlap with pollen limitation and total plant fitness measured; direct overlap-to-reproduction effect requires extraction from source data/figures.
notes: Stigmaphyllon paralias × oil-collecting bees; Brazil 2020. Strong contemporary explicit-overlap candidate.

title: Effects of pollinators herbivores and seed predators on flowering phenology
screening_reason: Classic synthesis/case study shows opposing temporal selective pressures but does not yet provide a single strict partner-synchrony effect under the IWE primary contract.
notes: Polemonium foliosissimum and Ipomopsis aggregata; retain as conceptual/empirical context for mutualist-antagonist timing trade-offs.

title: Timing of a plant-herbivore interaction alters plant growth and reproduction
screening_reason: Experiment directly manipulates timing of monarch herbivory and measures viable seed production but does not quantify synchrony with the natural antagonist activity window.
notes: Asclepias fascicularis × Danaus plexippus; candidate for predeclared direct-seasonal-timing sensitivity analysis rather than strict H1.

title: Induced phenological avoidance: A neglected defense mechanism against seed predation in plants
screening_reason: Direct predator activity window, flower timing, predation, and seed-mass fitness are measured in the same plants, but the fitness surface is nonlinear: predated plants maximize total seed mass at intermediate off-peak flowering rather than showing a single monotone synchrony slope.
notes: Geum urbanum × Byturus ochraceus; selfing host minimizes pollinator confounding. Dryad 10.5061/dryad.x3ffbg7dz. Admit to screening-informed shape/timing analysis, not strict linear H1.

title: Evolutionary trajectory of phenological escape in a flowering plant: Mechanistic insights from bidirectional avoidance of butterfly egg-laying pressure
screening_reason: Direct plant flowering schedules, butterfly egg-laying phenology, and realized fecundity are linked, with two temporal refugia on either side of the antagonist flight period; inherently bidirectional/nonlinear timing response.
notes: Cardamine pratensis × Anthocharis cardamines; larvae reduce realized fecundity strongly. Dryad 10.5061/dryad.v9s4mw741. Shape evidence, not a single linear H1 coefficient.

title: Consequences of variation in flowering phenology for seed head herbivory and reproductive success in Erigeron glaucus (Compositae)
screening_reason: Flowering synchrony, tephritid seed-head herbivory, and annual viable seed production are measured together; viable seed success is lowest at intermediate synchrony, demonstrating a nonlinear antagonist-associated fitness surface.
notes: Erigeron glaucus × Tephritis ovatipennis. Low-synchrony clones escape attack by extending flowering into fall; retain as shape evidence until quantitative curvature/variance is recovered.

title: The relationship between flowering phenology and selection in the wild sunflower Helianthus annuus
screening_reason: Seasonal abundance/damage of five seed-feeding herbivores and plant fitness were measured in the same population; mediation of apparent flowering-date selection by herbivore damage is strong, but no common-scale synchrony coefficient plus sampling variance has yet been recovered.
notes: Pilson 2000; strongest current strict-antagonist bridge candidate. Do not infer a meta effect from mediation alone.

title: Individual flowering rank and counteracting selection through pollination and predispersal seed predation in Vaccinium hirtum
screening_reason: Flowering rank, hand-pollination response, flower predation, seed predation and fitness were measured, but no single plant-partner overlap variable is identified.
notes: Mahoro 2002; multi-agent counterselection evidence from Kyoto populations.

title: Gender-specific consequences of a plant-pollinator mutualism: flowering phenology and nursery pollination in Chamaerops humilis
screening_reason: Flowering and pollinator emergence were monitored and fruit production was pollinator limited, but nursery costs occur mainly on male plants while pollination benefits accrue to females, preventing one individual-level net mixed fitness effect.
notes: Dufay 2010; informative timing/cost-benefit architecture, not strict net synchrony evidence.

title: Long-term variation in pollen limitation and predispersal seed predation in Ipomopsis aggregata
screening_reason: Long-term pollination limitation, seed-predator removal and demography are matched, but snowmelt/year rather than direct plant-partner synchrony is the timing exposure.
notes: Campbell et al. 2022; unusually strong null matched benefit/cost evidence.

title: Seed predation and flowering phenology in crop-wild sunflower hybrids
screening_reason: Flowering date strongly predicts some seed-damage classes and peak damage is seasonal, but independent animal activity and same-analysis final fitness are not both identified.
notes: Cummings et al. 1999; retain as antagonist timing context.

title: Seasonal counterselection by pollinators and pre-dispersal enemies in sequentially flowering Vaccinium congeners
screening_reason: Sequential congeners experience pollinator and enemy effects, but species differences and multiple agents prevent one partner-synchrony effect.
notes: Mahoro 2003; multi-agent context.

title: Flowering phenology and female fitness: Impact of a pre-dispersal seed predator on a sexually polymorphic species
screening_reason: Plant flowering onset, Hadena seed predation and final unattacked mature-seed fruit production were measured in the same plants in two years, but no independently quantified Hadena activity curve permits a strict plant-partner synchrony effect.
notes: Dianthus sylvestris × Hadena compta. Relative reproductive success slopes vs flowering onset: 2001 -0.037±0.009; 2003 -0.076±0.030. Post-freeze result was visible before holdout assignment, so this record is not shape-holdout confirmatory.

title: Do Flower Color and Floral Scent of Silene Species affect Host Preference of Hadena bicruris a Seed-Eating Pollinator under Field Conditions?
screening_reason: Field transplant scored flowering status and seed predation by Hadena, but the focal analysis is host preference/seed predation rather than temporal matching to final plant reproductive fitness.
notes: Page et al. 2014; useful post-freeze mixed candidate for source/citation closure, not strict H1.

title: The contribution of a pollinating seed predator to selection on Silene latifolia females
screening_reason: Hadena moth attack and female reproductive traits were followed and selection was partitioned into moth-attack and other components, but plant-partner synchrony is not the focal exposure.
notes: Burkhardt et al. 2012; strong mechanism/selection context. Post-freeze result was visible before any holdout assignment.
